prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Desktop Pet Controls", "Right-click your pet anywhere on screen to open quick settings, change behaviors, or minimize to the system tray.", "Right-click: Quick Menu | Double-click: Interact | Tray Icon: Restore/Hide"]
2: ["Choose Your Pet Experience", "Select photo creation to design a unique pet, or pick a classic pre-made companion.", "Photo AI vs Ready Template"]
3: ["Sign In to Protect Your Pet", "Signing in ensures your pet data, stats, and custom appearance are safely synced to the cloud.", "Automatic Cloud Save Enabled"]
4: ["You can always create additional custom pets or choose other companions later from your settings."]
5: ["Make sure to sign in with your main account to automatically recover existing pets and progress."]
6: ["Preparing desktop graphics engine and loading pet animations..."]
7: ["Pet missing? Look for the pet icon in your desktop system tray to bring it back to your screen."]
8: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion in 2 Minutes", "A quick setup to adopt or generate your personal desktop pet."]
9: ["Your desktop pet is now active! Click to say hello."]
